what: Louisiana-Pacific makes engineered wood products for building. Its main products are oriented strand board — structural panels used for roofs, walls and floors — and siding, the exterior cladding on a house, sold under the SmartSide brand.
customers: Homebuilders, repair and remodelling contractors, and building materials distributors and retailers across North America.
money: SmartSide engineered wood siding and trim, a branded product with better margins.
Structural panels, a commodity whose price swings violently.
South American operations and other products.
moat: Siding is the strategically important half: it is a branded, specified product that competes with vinyl and fibre cement on appearance and durability rather than on price, and it earns far better margins than panels. Oriented strand board is a pure commodity where the only advantage is having low-cost mills.
risks: Reported net income of $68.0M gives a price/earnings ratio of 75.7 and 171.1 times free cash flow — the earnings are at a cyclical trough.
Revenue collapsed from $3.9B in 2022 to $2.6B in 2023 as oriented strand board prices fell, showing how violent that commodity is.
Housing starts drive everything here, and they have been held down by mortgage rates.
At 23.5 times EV/EBITDA the price looks expensive, which is what a trough-earnings multiple looks like.
Fourteen analysts average an $87.86 target, about 20% above the current price.
opportunities: Debt of $378.0M against $292.0M of cash is a conservative balance sheet for a cyclical building products company.
The siding business is branded and specified, which gives it pricing power that commodity panels never have.
Engineered wood siding takes share from vinyl and fibre cement on appearance and durability.
American housing is under-supplied and the existing stock is old, which supports both new building and remodelling over time.
Operating leverage is substantial: when panel prices recover, almost all of the increase reaches profit.
watch: Siding revenue and margin, separately from oriented strand board. The siding business is what this company is worth; panels are the cycle.
view: Louisiana-Pacific has been trying for years to become a siding company that happens to make panels, rather than a panel company that happens to make siding, and the distinction is the whole investment case. Oriented strand board is a pure commodity: when housing is strong the price triples and the money is extraordinary, and when housing is weak the price collapses and so do the earnings. Revenue falling from $3.9 billion to $2.6 billion in a single year is that commodity doing what it does.

Siding is a different business. SmartSide is a branded, specified product that a builder or homeowner chooses over vinyl or fibre cement on appearance and durability, not on price per square foot. It earns better margins, the demand is driven as much by remodelling as by new construction, and it is not repriced weekly by a commodity market. The more of the company that is siding, the less the share price should swing.

The reported figures are currently unusable and should be set aside. A price/earnings ratio of 75.7 and 171 times free cash flow on $68 million of net income is what trough earnings look like, not what an expensive stock looks like. The same applies to 23.5 times EV/EBITDA. Anyone screening this on multiples will reach exactly the wrong conclusion in both directions — expensive at the bottom, cheap at the top.

What makes the trough survivable is the balance sheet: $378 million of debt against $292 million of cash is genuinely conservative for a cyclical building products company, and it means the company does not have to sell assets or raise equity to get through. The structural case is that American housing is under-supplied and the existing stock is old, so both new construction and remodelling demand arrive eventually. I would own this as a cyclical with a quality core, judged on siding revenue and margin, and I would ignore the headline multiples entirely.
bull: Siding keeps taking share from vinyl and fibre cement while housing recovers, and enormous operating leverage on panel prices lifts trough earnings sharply.
bear: Mortgage rates keep housing frozen for years, panel prices stay depressed, and siding growth is too small to offset the commodity half.
